questions.question: How do you pass query parameters and authentication in a Python HTTP request?
questions.title: Query Params and Authentication with requests
questions.direct_answer: Pass query parameters with the params= argument (a dict that requests encodes into the URL), and authentication via the auth= argument (e.g., HTTPBasicAuth for Basic auth) or the Authorization header directly (e.g., 'Bearer <token>' for JWT). params= is safer than string-concatenating the URL (it URL-encodes values correctly). For auth, prefer the auth= argument for Basic/Digest and set the Authorization header manually for bearer tokens and API keys; use environment variables or a secrets manager for credentials — never hardcode them.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you use params= (not string concatenation) for query strings and know the auth options (auth= for Basic, Authorization header for bearer/API keys), keeping credentials out of code.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: String-concatenating query params (encoding bugs) or hardcoding credentials in source (leaked in git).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: params= for query strings (auto-encoded); auth= for Basic, or the Authorization header for bearer tokens/API keys. Keep credentials in env vars, never hardcoded.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define Query Params and Authentication with requests simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Params and Auth the Safe Way
sections.content: In the requests library, pass query parameters with the params= argument as a dict — requests encodes them into the URL and properly URL-encodes special characters, which is safer than string-concatenating the URL yourself. For authentication, use the auth= argument for Basic and Digest auth (passing HTTPBasicAuth(user, pass)), or set the Authorization header directly for bearer tokens and API keys (headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer <token>'}). Keep credentials out of your code: load them from environment variables or a secrets manager, never hardcode them (they'd be committed to git and leaked). For OAuth flows, use an auth library like requests-oauthlib rather than hand-rolling the flow.

sections.title: How Params and Auth Are Attached
sections.content:
params becomes the query string; auth or the Authorization header carries credentials.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[params dict] -->|encoded| U[URL?name=Ada&page=2]
  A[auth= / Authorization header] -->|attached| Req[Authenticated request]
```

sections.title: Query params and two auth styles
sections.content:
```python
import requests
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth
import os

# (1) QUERY PARAMS: pass a dict; requests encodes them (and escapes specials).
r = requests.get('https://api.example.com/users',
                 params={'name': 'Ada Lovelace', 'page': 2})
#   -> GET https://api.example.com/users?name=Ada%20Lovelace&page=2

# (2) BASIC AUTH: use the auth= argument.
r = requests.get(url, auth=HTTPBasicAuth('user', os.environ['API_PASS']))

# (3) BEARER TOKEN (JWT) / API KEY: set the Authorization header.
token = os.environ['API_TOKEN']
r = requests.get(url, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'})
#   NEVER hardcode the token; load from env / secrets manager.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: String-concatenating query params — requests' params= encodes correctly; doing it by hand causes bugs.
Hardcoding credentials in source — they get committed to git and leaked; use env vars.
Putting the API key in the URL/query string where it's logged (use a header instead).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pass query params with params= (a dict); requests URL-encodes them — safer than string concatenation.
Basic auth: use auth=HTTPBasicAuth(user, pass); bearer/JWT: set the Authorization header.
Keep credentials in environment variables / secrets manager — never hardcoded in source.
Don't put API keys in the URL/query string (they get logged); use a header.
For OAuth flows, use requests-oauthlib rather than hand-rolling the signing/flow.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: In the requests library, pass query parameters with the params argument as a dict — requests encodes them into the URL and properly URL-encodes special characters, which is safer than string-concatenating the URL yourself. For authentication, use the auth argument for Basic and Digest auth by passing HTTPBasicAuth of user and pass, or set the Authorization header directly for bearer tokens and API keys. Keep credentials out of your code: load them from environment variables or a secrets manager, never hardcode them, because hardcoded credentials get committed to git and leaked. For OAuth flows, use an auth library like requests-oauthlib rather than hand-rolling the signing and the flow. And don't put API keys in the URL or query string where they get logged in server logs and proxy caches — use a header instead.
